## Dates

Each commit is dated at noon (America/Sao_Paulo) on the day the change took effect. The other dates, enacted and published, are trailers.

When a law gives no date of its own, the default rule applies: Decreto-Lei 4.657/1942 (LINDB) art. 1: 'Salvo disposição contrária, a lei começa a vigorar em todo o país quarenta e cinco dias depois de oficialmente publicada'; the period is counted under LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1 (publication day and last day included, in force the day after). https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/decreto-lei/del4657compilado.htm

## How the history is built

`tools/build.py` turns the corpus into this history in one pass: one commit per law, on the day it took effect. The same corpus always gives the same commit hashes. `tools/check_repo.py` reads every version back from git and compares it with the corpus. `tools/on.py` shows the law as it stood on any date. The corpus format is described in `tools/SCHEMA.md`.

## Decisions made by hand

- Every Planalto (www.planalto.gov.br) page is read from a dated Internet Archive capture, byte-for-byte what Planalto served.
- The Constitution's history is rebuilt from Planalto's annotated page (constituicao.htm), which keeps every superseded wording struck through beside its replacement, each with the source's own note ('Redação dada pela', 'Incluído pela', 'Revogado pela', 'Renumerado'). Text with no note is the 1988 original.
- A paragraph starts on the in-force day of the amendment in its note; a struck paragraph ends on the in-force day of its 'Revogado pela' note, else when the next wording of the same dispositivo in the same article starts. Counts of how struck paragraphs were ended: {'court': 1, 'duplicate': 9, 'future': 1, 'heading-rename': 7, 'note': 54, 'parent': 231, 'renumbered': 4, 'same-day-twin': 1, 'successor': 463}.
- 'parent': a struck paragraph with no note and no later wording is taken to have fallen with the nearest struck enclosing dispositivo (for example the items of an article revoked as a whole).
- 'duplicate': Planalto sometimes keeps a struck copy of a block next to the same text unstruck (renumbered or re-marked); such a struck copy is never shown.
- 'renumbered': a struck 'Parágrafo único' followed by an unannotated '§ 1º' became § 1º when an amendment added § 2º to the article; the date and credit are those of the § 2º's own 'Incluído pela' note.
- A line with no note inside an article that did not exist in 1988 (every caput of the article carries an amendment note) is dated and credited by the article's first caput (one line: ADCT art. 126 I).
- Art. 246 was inserted, word for word, by both EC 6/1995 and EC 7/1995 on the same day; Planalto shows it twice. It is one line, credited to both.
- Heading renames that Planalto shows without a note are dated and credited by the amendment whose text renames them (checked at parse time): 'DOS SERVIDORES PÚBLICOS CIVIS' -> 'DOS SERVIDORES PÚBLICOS' (Emenda Constitucional nº 18, de 1998); 'DOS TRIBUNAIS E JUÍZES DO TRABALHO' -> 'Do Tribunal Superior do Trabalho, dos Tribunais Regionais do Trabalho e dos Juízes do Trabalho' (Emenda Constitucional nº 92, de 2016); 'DA CIÊNCIA E TECNOLOGIA' -> 'DA CIÊNCIA, TECNOLOGIA E INOVAÇÃO' (Emenda Constitucional nº 85, de 2015); 'DA FAMÍLIA, DA CRIANÇA, DO ADOLESCENTE E DO IDOSO' -> 'Da Família, da Criança, do Adolescente, do Jovem e do Idoso' (Emenda Constitucional nº 65, de 2010); 'DOS SERVIDORES PÚBLICOS MILITARES' -> 'DOS MILITARES DOS ESTADOS, DO DISTRITO FEDERAL E DOS TERRITÓRIOS' (Emenda Constitucional nº 18, de 1998); 'DA ADVOCACIA-GERAL DA UNIÃO' -> 'DA ADVOCACIA PÚBLICA' (Emenda Constitucional nº 19, de 1998); 'DA ADVOCACIA E DA DEFENSORIA PÚBLICA' -> 'Da Advocacia' (Emenda Constitucional nº 80, de 2014).
- EC 126/2022 art. 9 revoked ADCT arts. 106, 107, 109, 110, 111, 111-A, 112 and 114 'após a sanção da lei complementar prevista no art. 6º'; that is LC 200/2023, sanctioned 30.8.2023 and published 31.8.2023 (Planalto lcp200.htm), so those revocations are dated 2023-08-31.
- STF judged ADI 7047 (with ADI 7064) in the virtual session of 30.11.2023 and excluded the expression 'com auto aplicabilidade para a União' from art. 100 § 11 (EC 113/2021 wording); the minutes (ata de julgamento) were published in the DJE on 04.12.2023, the day the ruling binds all. Planalto shows the expression struck, linked to the case. The same ruling declared art. 100 § 9º and ADCT art. 101 § 5º (EC 113/2021 wording) unconstitutional, but Planalto leaves their words in place with a 'Vide ADI' note, so the ruling is credited to ADCT art. 101 with its words unchanged, and art. 100 § 9º keeps its words.
- 'Vide ADI' notes are informational and change no text; only a ruling that Planalto shows as struck words is a court law here.
- Future text: Planalto's Constitution page shows wording enacted but not yet in force only as 'Vide ... Vigência' notes beside the text in force. EC 141/2026 art. 10, I: the change to art. 7 XV enters into force 'após decorridos 2 (dois) meses de sua publicação' (DOU 16.10.2026); counting as LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1 does for days (publication day included, in force the day after the period), that is 16.12.2026. The new wording is read from EC 141's own text. EC 132/2023's changes that take effect in 2027 and 2033 (its art. 23: arts. 3, 4, 5 and 11) are not on the future branch yet.
- Units: one file per article (art-NNN, ADCT adct-art-NNN), plus the preamble and one file each for the headings of the main text and of the ADCT (titulos, adct-titulos). Each paragraph or item is one line; notes are removed; the signatures are left out.

- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Where Planalto repeats an older wording after an MP wording (an MP provision that lapsed or that the conversion law dropped), the repeated wording is dated from the day the MP wording ended.
- Revocations by a Medida Provisória that lapsed are gaps: the text is out of force from the MP's day to the lapse and back afterwards, credited to a separate '<MP>: vigência encerrada' record that restores it.
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).

- Rules for struck text with no note of its own, each in the source's layout: 'run-revoked' - an earlier line of a struck run closed by one 'Revogado pela' note; 'heads' - a struck rubrica falls with the dispositivo it heads; 'date-order' - wordings of one dispositivo printed out of date order (CP art. 121 § 7º II) are chained by their own dates; a '(VETADO)' item left unstruck above wording promulgated over the veto ends on the promulgation (Lei 13.964/2019: DOU 30.4.2021); a 'Parágrafo único' left unstruck above a '§ 1º' that a later law's note introduces ends when the § 1º starts.

- Clauses counted in months or years: from LC 107/2001 (26.4.2001) on, the period ends on the same calendar day and the law is in force the day after (LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1); before it, by Lei 810/1949 the law is in force on the corresponding day (Lei 7.209/1984: published 13.7.1984, in force 13.1.1985). Clauses in days: publication day + N for every period.

- A wording ends no later than the next wording of the same dispositivo (also a wording a law in force on the act's first day rewrote that day), even where the source also notes a later revocation; the lines under it (its incisos, alíneas, penalties) that ended with it end with it: codigo-penal art-216 [Parágrafo único] 2009-08-10 -> 2005-03-29; codigo-de-processo-civil art-0988 [§ 5º] 2026-09-03 -> 2016-03-18; codigo-de-processo-civil art-1042 [Art. 1.042] 2026-09-03 -> 2016-03-18; codigo-de-processo-civil art-1042 [§ 2º] 2026-09-03 -> 2016-03-18.
- Twin wordings: a line printed below a struck line of the same dispositivo with the same start, word for word the same or (with no note of its own) a new wording, starts on the first day from the struck line's end on when no other wording of that dispositivo stands, or with the restored caput of its article; a struck lower copy that never stands alone is left out: codigo-penal art-272 [Modalidade culposa] from 1998-07-03; codigo-penal art-273 [Modalidade culposa] from 1998-07-03; codigo-penal art-273 [§ 2º] from 1998-07-03.
- CLT (Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (Decreto-Lei nº 5.452, de 1º de maio de 1943)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (del5452.htm): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (Decreto-Lei nº 5.452, de 1º de maio de 1943): in force 1943-11-10 (Decreto-Lei 5.452/1943 art. 2: 'O presente decreto-lei entrará em vigor em 10 de novembro de 1943' (published in the DOU of 9.8.1943)).
- Headings (Parte, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- The CLT is the annex of Decreto-Lei 5.452/1943: the decree's own text (ementa, arts. 1 and 2) is the file preambulo.md, the Consolidação starts at its heading 'CONSOLIDAÇÃO DAS LEIS DO TRABALHO', and the closing 'ANEXO' (the table of economic and professional categories art. 577 refers to) is one file, anexo.md, one table cell per line in page order.
- Planalto's note forms read as starts: 'Redação dada', 'Incluído' (and the misspellings 'Incuído', 'Inlcuído'), 'Acrescido', 'Renumerado', 'Redação restabelecida', 'Restabelecido', 'Restaurado', 'Revigorado', 'Corrigido'; as ends: 'Revogado', 'Suprimido', 'Extinto', 'Fica sem efeito'. 'Vide' notes change nothing.
- 'com vigência suspensa pelo Decreto-lei nº 8.987-A, de 1946': the wording Decreto-Lei 8.740/1946 gave ends when 8.987-A took effect; a revocation by 8.740 is a gap that 8.987-A closed; a wording 'restabelecida' by 8.987-A that Planalto prints only once is also the 1943 wording, in force before 8.740 took effect. A change suspended before it took effect is left out of the history.
- One note on art. 457-A, III is broken over two paragraphs and lacks the act's number ('(Incluído pela Medida Provisória nº' / ', de 2019)'); both halves link to mpv905.htm, so it is read as MP 905/2019.
- A struck cross-reference link inside an unstruck wording (art. 329 'art. 325', art. 442-B 'art. 3º desta Consolidação') is a typesetting slip: the consolidated page prints it unstruck, and so does the history.
- Pages that print no Diário Oficial date (some 1940s decree-laws give only the Coleção das Leis do Brasil, an annual compilation): the enactment day stands in for the publication day: Decreto-Lei nº 5.922, de 1943 (enacted 1943-10-25); Decreto-Lei nº 6.053, de 1943 (enacted 1943-11-30); Decreto-Lei nº 8.080, de 1945 (enacted 1945-10-11); Lei nº 6.514, de 1977 (enacted 1977-12-22).
- Some laws are in force on one day but defer the effects of some provisions ('produzirá efeitos'); a change is dated by the day it takes effect where the clause fixes a later day for it (the effect-days decision lists the units moved); effects that are retroactive, financial only or left to a later act or condition keep the in-force day. - A wording ends no later than the next wording of the same dispositivo (also a wording a law in force on the act's first day rewrote that day), even where the source also notes a later revocation; the lines under it (its incisos, alíneas, penalties) that ended with it end with it: clt art-896 [Art. 896] 1954-06-30 -> 1949-10-21.
- A caput printed 'Artigo N - ...' is read as that article's caput: clt art-896 'Artigo 896 -'.
- A line with no note of its own, printed unstruck under an unstruck line a later law inserted ('Incluído'), starts with it where an older wording under the same label is printed struck in the article: clt art-678 [a)] from 1968-05-28; clt art-678 [b)] from 1968-05-28; clt art-678 [c)] from 1968-05-28; clt art-678 [d)] from 1968-05-28; clt art-894 [b)] from 2007-09-23.

- Acts of this part (Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei nº 3.689, de 3 de outubro de 1941), Código de Defesa do Consumidor (Lei nº 8.078, de 11 de setembro de 1990)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (del3689.htm, l8078.htm): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).

- Headings (Parte, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- Código de Processo Penal: the page's alignment is unreliable (heading name lines are often not centred), so headings are only Livro/Título/Capítulo/Seção lines, the name line right after one, and lines in capitals without a comma (as for the Código Penal).
- Rules for struck text with no note of its own, each in the source's layout: 'run-revoked' - an earlier line of a struck run closed by one 'Revogado pela' note; 'heads' - a struck rubrica or heading falls with the struck dispositivo after it; 'heading-reworded' - a struck heading block followed, after struck articles, by the same heading reworded (CPP Capítulo V 'DAS PERGUNTAS AO OFENDIDO' -> 'DO OFENDIDO', Lei 11.690/2008) ends when the new block's note starts it; a struck '(VETADO)' line directly above wording a law's promulgated vetoed parts introduced stands from that law's day to the promulgation; the successor of a struck wording may lie past a heading reworded between the two wordings.
- Typesetting slips read as unstruck: a struck ordinal sign or full stop inside unstruck text ('§ 1<strike>º</strike>', CDC art. 8; CPP arts. 312 and 313) and a struck cross-reference link (CPP art. 336: '(art. 110 do Código Penal)'); a strike that ends inside the last word of a struck wording (CPP art. 725 III: '... como tam</strike>bem ao juiz') is read as struck. A run of full stops left at the end of a line by removed notes becomes one full stop. 'Il - no concurso' (CPP art. 78) is read as the label 'II -'; 'Parágrafo Único' as 'Parágrafo único' (the text keeps the source's spelling).
- Unstruck '(Revogado)' placeholders of the annotated page ('Parágrafo único. (Revogado).') stay in the text as Planalto prints them; the check ignores placeholder lines on both pages, since the consolidated page prints a placeholder ('IV - (revogado).', 'Art. 556. a Art. 560') where the annotated page keeps the struck wording.
- Text before its law: every line is dated by the in-force day of the law in its own note, so no wording appears before the law that made it; the parser checks this for every line with a 'Redação dada', 'Incluído' or 'Renumerado' note (see the count below). Court rulings Planalto shows only as 'Vide ADI ...' notes (the Lei 13.964/2019 juiz das garantias articles, ADI 6.298, 6.299, 6.300 and 6.305, among others) change no words on the page, so the history has no commit for them.

- Effect days (produção de efeitos): where an act fixes a later day from which a provision produces effects ('produzindo efeitos a partir de ...'), the change is dated by that day, not by the act's in-force day (dates after 2026-10-31 are on the future branch); hunks a later act replaced before their effect day never took effect. Applied by Lexifina's code after the replay. Medida Provisória 689/2015 art. 3: 'produzindo efeitos a partir do primeiro dia do quarto mês subsequente ao de sua publicação' (DOU 31.8.2015): from 1.12.2015, until the MP lapsed. - Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).

- Lei de Abuso de Autoridade: the parts of Lei 13.869/2019 vetoed on 5.9.2019 were promulgated after Congress overrode the veto (DOU 27.9.2019, edição extra), before the act took effect on 3.1.2020, so they are part of its first version and the '(VETADO)' lines never stood.
- Lei Geral do Esporte: Congress overrode vetoes of Lei 14.597/2023 and the President promulgated those parts on 21.5.2024 (DOU 22.5.2024; the text is printed at the end of Planalto's page): each promulgated dispositivo (arts. 15, 27 parágrafo único, 34 parágrafo único, 36 § 1º, 37, 40 to 49 with the headings of Seções II and III of their chapter, 86 § 12, 153, 160 § 1º, 212 and the others the promulgation text names) takes effect on 22.5.2024, credited to Lei 14.597/2023, and its '(VETADO)' line stands until then.
- Lei do Petróleo, Lei 12.734/2012: its art. 3 (the new wordings of arts. 48, 49 and 50 and the new arts. 49-A to 49-C and 50-A to 50-F) and its art. 4 (revoking art. 49 §§ 1º to 3º and art. 50 § 4º) were vetoed when the law was sanctioned (DOU 30.11.2012); Congress overrode the veto and the parts were promulgated on 14.3.2013 (DOU 15.3.2013; promulgation text on Lei 12.734's page), so every Lei 12.734 wording of this act takes effect on 15.3.2013 (art. 5: in force on publication), credited to Lei 12.734/2012, and the wordings it replaced stand until then; Planalto's annotated page of Lei 9.478 does not give that day. Lei 12.734's page notes a partial republication on 25.3.2013; the history uses the wordings Planalto prints.
- Lei do Petróleo, Medida Provisória nº 592/2012 (in force 3.12.2012, lapsed 13.5.2013): its art. 3 I and II revoked art. 49 § 3º and art. 50 § 4º (Planalto's page gives them only '(Vide Medida Provisória nº 592, 2012)'), so those paragraphs end on 3.12.2012, credited to it (Lei 12.734 revoked them again from 15.3.2013, so the lapse does not restore them); the MP's arts. 49-A, 50 § 5º, 50-A and 50-B end on 15.3.2013, when Lei 12.734's wordings of the same dispositivos take effect; its arts. 48-A and 81-A stand until the lapse.
- Lei do Petróleo: STF, ADI 4.917, medida cautelar of 18.3.2013 (Min. Cármen Lúcia, ad referendum; DJe 21.3.2013; read from the case's record of proceedings) suspended the effects of arts. 48 II, 49 II, 49-A to 49-C, 50 § 2º and 50-A to 50-E as worded by Lei 12.734/2012 until the final judgment, still pending when the data was read. - Acts of this part (Lei de Execução Fiscal (Lei nº 6.830, de 22 de setembro de 1980); Lei de Defesa da Concorrência (Lei nº 12.529, de 30 de novembro de 2011); Estatuto da Advocacia e da OAB (Lei nº 8.906, de 4 de julho de 1994); Lei da ADI e da ADC (Lei nº 9.868, de 10 de novembro de 1999); Lei da ADPF (Lei nº 9.882, de 3 de dezembro de 1999); Crimes contra a ordem tributária, econômica e as relações de consumo (Lei nº 8.137, de 27 de dezembro de 1990); Lei de Interceptação Telefônica (Lei nº 9.296, de 24 de julho de 1996); Lei do Bem de Família (Lei nº 8.009, de 29 de março de 1990); Lei da Ação Popular (Lei nº 4.717, de 29 de junho de 1965); Crimes contra o Sistema Financeiro Nacional (Lei nº 7.492, de 16 de junho de 1986)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l6830.htm, l12529.htm, l8906.htm, l9868.htm, l9882.htm, l8137.htm, l9296.htm, l8009.htm, l4717.htm, l7492.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).

- Lei dos Planos de Saúde: from 5.6.1998 (Medida Provisória nº 1.665, issued before the act took effect on 2.9.1998) to 27.8.2001 the act was rewritten by a chain of about 44 monthly reissued Medidas Provisórias (1.665, 1.685, 1.730, 1.801, 1.908, 1.976, 2.097 and 2.177), the last being MP 2.177-44 (DOU 27.8.2001), kept in force by EC 32/2001 art. 2. Planalto's page prints only the 1998 text and MP 2.177-44's wording and cites the earlier reissues with 'Vide' notes, so the text in force from 1998 to 2001 cannot be rebuilt from it. The history therefore starts on 27.8.2001 with the oldest version available (the act as MP 2.177-44 worded it, including Lei 10.223/2001's change), credited to the publisher; the 1998 text and the monthly reissues are not modelled.

- Acts of this part (Lei das Contravenções Penais (Decreto-Lei nº 3.688, de 3 de outubro de 1941); Lei dos Crimes de Responsabilidade (Lei nº 1.079, de 10 de abril de 1950); Crimes resultantes de preconceito de raça ou de cor (Lei nº 7.716, de 5 de janeiro de 1989)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (del3688.htm, l1079.htm, l7716.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Lei das Contravenções Penais (Decreto-Lei nº 3.688, de 3 de outubro de 1941): in force 1942-01-01 (Decreto-Lei 3.688/1941 art. 72: 'Esta lei entrará em vigor no dia 1º de janeiro de 1942').
- Lei dos Crimes de Responsabilidade (Lei nº 1.079, de 10 de abril de 1950): in force 1950-05-27 (Lei 1.079/1950 has no vigência clause (its last article, art. 82, sets the time limit for the trial): LINDB art. 1, 45 days after publication in the DOU of 12.4.1950).

- Life spans set by hand where Planalto's page cannot give them (Medidas Provisórias revoked, suspended by the STF or converted without the change): Lei do Sistema Financeiro Nacional art. 10 IV: Planalto prints the former inciso III struck as inciso IV, noted 'Renumerado pela Lei nº 7.730'; Medida Provisória nº 32/1989 (16.1.1989) and Lei 7.730/1989, its conversion, gave inciso IV a new wording in the same act, so the renumbered words never stood as inciso IV and are left out; Lei do Sistema Financeiro Nacional art. 42: Medida Provisória nº 784/2017 revoked the whole article (8.6.2017 to its lapse, 20.10.2017) before Lei 13.506/2017 did (14.11.2017); Planalto notes the MP only on the caput, so the quoted wording of Lei 1.808/1953 art. 2 the article carries is absent with it while the MP stood.
- A wording ends no later than the next wording of the same dispositivo (also a wording a law in force on the act's first day rewrote that day), even where the source also notes a later revocation; the lines under it (its incisos, alíneas, penalties) that ended with it end with it: lei-do-sistema-financeiro-nacional art-35 [Parágrafo único] 2017-11-14 -> 1986-11-24.
- Twin wordings: a line printed below a struck line of the same dispositivo with the same start, word for word the same or (with no note of its own) a new wording, starts on the first day from the struck line's end on when no other wording of that dispositivo stands, or with the restored caput of its article; a struck lower copy that never stands alone is left out: lei-do-sistema-financeiro-nacional art-04 [a)] from 1970-02-19; lei-do-sistema-financeiro-nacional art-04 [b)] from 1970-02-19; lei-do-sistema-financeiro-nacional art-04 [a)] from 1977-10-18; lei-do-sistema-financeiro-nacional art-04 [b)] from 1977-10-18.

- Acts of this part (Lei Kandir - ICMS (Lei Complementar nº 87, de 13 de setembro de 1996); Lei do ISS (Lei Complementar nº 116, de 31 de julho de 2003)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (lcp87.htm, lcp116.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).

- Headings (Parte, Livro, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- No OCR: every text comes from the HTML text layer of the Planalto pages.
- Some laws are in force on one day but defer the effects of some provisions ('produzirá efeitos'); a change is dated by the day it takes effect where the clause fixes a later day for it (the effect-days decision lists the units moved); effects that are retroactive, financial only or left to a later act or condition keep the in-force day. - Label slips read as the label they stand for: Estatuto da Microempresa art. 18 § 1º-A: Planalto prints the label '§ 1º A.' (no hyphen); filed as § 1º-A, the text kept as printed.
- Life spans set by hand where Planalto's page cannot give them (Medidas Provisórias revoked, suspended by the STF or converted without the change): Estatuto da Microempresa art. 18-A § 3º V: Planalto prints bare 'd)' and 'e)' lines carrying only '(Vide Lei Complementar nº 214, de 2025)' pointers, without their wording (alíneas Lei Complementar 214/2025 adds for later years); they are left out; Estatuto da Microempresa arts. 18-C, 38-A and 85-A: the articles are in the republished text (their caput carries no 'Incluído' note), so their lines without a note belong to the oldest version available, not to the first law noted inside the article (the rule for articles inserted after the act).
- A lettered article (inserted after enactment) whose 'Incluído' note Planalto prints only on its last line: its unnoted lines take that note's law and day (art-18-c: 10 lines by Lei Complementar nº 147, de 2014; art-38-a: 4 lines by Lei Complementar nº 214, de 2025; art-85-a: 5 lines by Lei Complementar nº 147, de 2014).

- Lei Complementar nº 169, de 2019: in force 2020-05-31, own clause: 180 days after publication (2019-12-03; LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1).
- Lei Complementar nº 182, de 2021: in force 2021-08-31, own clause: 90 days after publication (2021-06-02; LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1).
- Lei Complementar nº 188, de 2021: in force 2021-12-31, art. 3: 'Esta Lei Complementar entra em vigor na data de sua publicação' (DOU 31.12.2021, edição extra; the page's heading 'Nº 188, 31 DE DEZEMBRO DE 2021' lacks 'DE', so the day is set here).
- Lei Complementar nº 216, de 2025: in force 2025-07-29, art. 8: 'Esta Lei Complementar entra em vigor: I - em 1º de janeiro de 2026, quanto à parte do art. 4º que inclui o inciso I no caput do art. 12-A da Lei nº 11.945 [...]; e II - na data de sua publicação, quanto aos demais dispositivos' (DOU 29.7.2025); its change to the Estatuto da Microempresa (art. 2) falls under II.

- Effect days (produção de efeitos): where an act fixes a later day from which a provision produces effects ('produzindo efeitos a partir de ...'), the change is dated by that day, not by the act's in-force day (dates after 2026-10-31 are on the future branch); hunks a later act replaced before their effect day never took effect. - Acts of this part (Lei Orgânica da Seguridade Social - custeio (Lei nº 8.212, de 24 de julho de 1991)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l8212cons.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Lei Orgânica da Seguridade Social - custeio (Lei nº 8.212, de 24 de julho de 1991): in force 1991-07-25 (Lei 8.212/1991 art. 104: 'Esta Lei entrará em vigor na data de sua publicação' (DOU 25.7.1991, republished 11.4.1996 and 14.8.1998)).
- Headings (Parte, Livro, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- No OCR: every text comes from the HTML text layer of the Planalto pages.
- Lines with no label and no note ('Pena - ...', table rows) start with the dispositivo above them when it is a new one ('Incluído') or when an earlier unlabeled line of the article was replaced with it (8): LOSS art-020 'Salário-de-contribuição' from 1995-04-29; LOSS art-020 'Alíquota em %' from 1995-04-29; LOSS art-020 'até 249,80' from 1995-04-29; LOSS art-020 '8,00' from 1995-04-29; LOSS art-020 'de 249,81 até 416,33' from 1995-04-29; LOSS art-020 '9,00' from 1995-04-29; LOSS art-020 'de 416,34 até 832,66' from 1995-04-29; LOSS art-020 '11,00' from 1995-04-29.
- Some laws are in force on one day but defer the effects of some provisions ('produzirá efeitos'); a change is dated by the day it takes effect where the clause fixes a later day for it (the effect-days decision lists the units moved); effects that are retroactive, financial only or left to a later act or condition keep the in-force day. - Resolução do Senado Federal nº 26, de 21.6.2005 (DOU 22.6.2005), art. 1: 'É suspensa a execução da alínea "h" do inciso I do art. 12 da Lei Federal nº 8.212 [...] em virtude de declaração de inconstitucionalidade em decisão definitiva do Supremo Tribunal Federal, nos autos do Recurso Extraordinário nº 351.717-1'; art. 2: in force on publication. Lei 8.212 art. 12 I h) (added by Lei 9.506/1997) ends on 22.6.2005, credited to the resolution (kind law: a Senate act).
- Resolução do Senado Federal nº 10, de 30.3.2016 (DOU 31.3.2016), art. 1: 'É suspensa, nos termos do art. 52, inciso X, da Constituição Federal, a execução do inciso IV do art. 22 da Lei nº 8.212 [...] declarado inconstitucional por decisão definitiva proferida pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal nos autos do Recurso Extraordinário nº 595.838'; art. 2: in force on publication. Lei 8.212 art. 22 IV (added by Lei 9.876/1999) ends on 31.3.2016, credited to the resolution (kind law: a Senate act).
- Resolução do Senado Federal nº 15, de 12.9.2017 (DOU 13.9.2017), art. 1: 'É suspensa [...] a execução do inciso VII do art. 12 da Lei nº 8.212 [...] e a execução do art. 1º da Lei nº 8.540 [...], que deu nova redação ao art. 12, inciso V, ao art. 25, incisos I e II, e ao art. 30, inciso IV, da Lei nº 8.212 [...], todos com a redação atualizada até a Lei nº 9.528, de 10 de dezembro de 1997, declarados inconstitucionais [...] nos autos do Recurso Extraordinário nº 363.852'; art. 2: in force on publication. Planalto notes the suspension beside the struck wordings of art. 12 V (and its alíneas), art. 12 VII and art. 25 I. Of these only art. 25 I (Lei 9.528/1997's wording, '2% da receita bruta [...]') was still the text in 2017: it ends on 13.9.2017, credited to the resolution, and the inciso is absent until Lei 13.606/2018 gave it a new wording (10.1.2018); the others had been replaced by Leis 9.876/1999 and 11.718/2008 and are unchanged. Planalto prints no note at art. 25 II, which is kept. Medida Provisória 793/2017's wording of art. 25 I ('1,2%'; DOU 1.8.2017) was to produce effects from 1.1.2018 (its art. 14 I, for its art. 12) and the MP lapsed on 28.11.2017, so it never applied and is left out (as the effect-day rule requires).

- Lei 8.212: Planalto's annotated page keeps the numbered footnote markers of a 1998 edition (50 superscript numbers such as 'e) as importâncias: 14'); the footnotes themselves (on Medidas Provisórias then pending, and updated amounts) are printed after the signature, outside the act, so the markers are dropped from the text and the footnotes are not part of the history.
- Lei 8.212: Planalto's pages set each Título and Capítulo name as an unaligned paragraph inside a centred block (only the 'TÍTULO I' line itself is centred text); these names are read as heading lines, as displayed, not as marginal headings of the following article.
- Lei 8.212 arts. 20, 26, 36, 68 and 94: Planalto's annotated page prints only later wordings of these articles, not their 1991 text; the 1991 wording is read from Planalto's page of the act as enacted (L8212orig.htm, which strikes it above the later wording; for art. 94 it prints it unstruck) and placed struck above the first wording the annotated page prints, which ends it (art. 36: revoked by Lei 8.218/1991): art-006 § 10 (text of a line printed as its bare label), art-020 (10 lines), art-026 (1 lines), art-036 (1 lines), art-068 (1 lines), art-094 (1 lines).
- Tables printed inside articles (ctx:l8212-original 4, l8212 6, l8212-compilado 3): Planalto centres their cells; each cell is a line of the article it is printed in (as in the CLT's art. 580), not a heading line.
- Articles Planalto prints with the letter but no hyphen ('Art. 22A.', 'Art. 22B.', 'Art. 25A.') are articles of their own (art-022-a, ...), labelled 'Art. 22-A' like the rest of the corpus: art-022-a, art-022-b, art-025-a.
- Misprints corrected: Lei 8.212 Capítulo VI heading (Lei 8.398/1992): Planalto's annotated page misprints 'Pescado}'; the consolidated page reads 'DO PESCADOR'; Lei 8.212 art. 30 § 2º II (Lei 13.202/2015): the annotated page drops the closing period, which Lei 13.202's own text and the consolidated page print; Lei 8.212 Título VII heading: the annotated page prints a stray 'l' after 'TÍTULO VII' (the consolidated page does not); Lei 8.212 art. 93: the note '(Revogado o caput pela Lei nº 9.639, de 25.5.98.)', whose inner period kept it in the text, is read as the caput's revocation note.
- A period printed after an amendment note that follows a line already ending in ';', ':' or ',' ('... salário-maternidade; (Redação dada pela Lei nº 9.528, de 10.12.97).') closes the note and is dropped with it (lines: ctx:l8212-original 25, l8212 164, l8212-compilado 95).
- Life spans set by hand for these acts: Lei 8.212 art. 55: Planalto prints the whole article twice, first with the caput's note 'Revogado pela Medida Provisória nº 446, de 2008' (MP 446 was rejected on 10.2.2009), then again with every line noted 'Revogado pela Lei nº 12.101, de 2009' (30.11.2009); the first copy is the article, all of it out of force while MP 446 stood (10.11.2008 to 10.2.2009), and the second copy (the same wordings) is left out; Lei 8.212 art. 25 I (Lei 9.528/1997's wording, '2% da receita bruta [...]') is printed above the caput Lei 10.256/2001 gave the article and is placed after that caput, under which it stood until 13.9.2017; Lei 8.212 art. 20's rate table: the 1991 table (original page) stands to Lei 9.032/1995 (29.4.1995), Lei 9.032's table (original page; 'até R$ 249,80 [...] até R$ 836,90') to Lei 9.129/1995 (21.11.1995), and the table the annotated page prints ('até 249,80 [...] até 832,66', followed there by '(Valores e alíquotas dados pela Lei nº 9.129, de 20.11.95)', and in Lei 9.129's own text) from then.
- Lei 8.212 (open items): Planalto's 'Vide' pointers (ADIs 2.028, 2.036, 2.228, 4.395, 5.161, 7.633; Lei Complementar 150/2015; Lei 15.371/2026) strike no words and are not modelled; the amounts of the art. 20 and art. 21 tables updated by ministerial portarias are not part of the act's text.
- Life spans set by hand where Planalto's page cannot give them (Medidas Provisórias revoked, suspended by the STF or converted without the change): Lei 8.212 art. 26: Planalto prints the 1992 wording (Lei 8.436/1992) of the caput and §§ 1º-3º, then Medida Provisória 841/2018's wording (lapsed 23.10.2018), then the 1992 wording again (in force again from 24.10.2018 to Lei 13.756/2018, 13.12.2018); the second copy of §§ 1º-3º starts on 24.10.2018, like the caput's; Lei 8.212 art. 39 caput: Lei 8.620/1993's wording ends when Lei 11.098/2005's starts (14.1.2005, see its in-force day); Medida Provisória 258/2005 replaced that wording from 15.8.2005 until it lapsed (18.11.2005), so Lei 11.098's wording stands from 14.1.2005 to Lei 11.457/2007 (2.5.2007) except from 15.8.2005 to 18.11.2005 (Planalto prints MP 258's wording above Lei 11.098's); Lei 8.212 art. 44: Planalto prints the 1991 wording, Medida Provisória 258/2005's wording (lapsed 18.11.2005), the 1991 wording again and Lei 8.620/1993's wording (revoked by Lei 11.501/2007). The wording in force when MP 258 came and again after its lapse was Lei 8.620's, so it stands from 6.1.1993 to 12.7.2007 except from 15.8.2005 to 18.11.2005, and the second copy of the 1991 wording (a reprint, no note) is left out; Lei 8.212 art. 50 caput: Planalto prints Lei 9.476/1997's wording struck (replaced by Medida Provisória 449/2008, 4.12.2008), then MP 449's caput and §§ 1º-2º, then the 1991 wording, Lei 8.620/1993's, and Lei 9.476's wording again unstruck: Lei 11.941/2009, MP 449's conversion, did not take up MP 449's art. 50, so Lei 9.476's wording is in force again from 28.5.2009. - Twin wordings: a line printed below a struck line of the same dispositivo with the same start, word for word the same or (with no note of its own) a new wording, starts on the first day from the struck line's end on when no other wording of that dispositivo stands, or with the restored caput of its article; a struck lower copy that never stands alone is left out: lei-de-custeio-da-seguridade-social art-080 [I -] from 2004-06-21.

- Medidas Provisórias and their fate, from each MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line or the Congress records: Medida Provisória nº 1.002, de 1995 (in force 1995-05-22) was converted into Lei nº 9.063, de 1995 (in force 1995-06-20); Medida Provisória nº 1.093, de 2021 (in force 2021-12-31) was converted into Lei nº 14.360, de 2022 (in force 2022-06-02); Medida Provisória nº 1.107, de 2022 (in force 2022-03-18) was converted into Lei nº 14.438, de 2022 (in force 2022-08-25); Medida Provisória nº 1.110, de 2022 (in force 2022-03-28) lapsed: Ato Declaratório do Presidente da Mesa do Congresso Nacional nº 65, de 2022 (DOU 19.8.2022): 'teve seu prazo de vigência encerrado no dia 7 de agosto'; Medida Provisória nº 1.202, de 2023 (in force 2023-12-29) was converted into Lei nº 14.873, de 2024 (in force 2024-05-29); Medida Provisória nº 2.170, de 2001 (in force 2001-08-24) stands: Medida Provisória nº 2.170-36, de 23.8.2001 (DOU 24.8.2001, in force on publication; its effects from 1.1.1999 are retroactive, so its changes are dated by publication), kept in force by Emenda Constitucional 32/2001, art. 2; its art. 8 revoked Lei 8.212 art. 60 parágrafo único; Medida Provisória nº 2.187, de 2001 (in force 2001-08-27) stands: Medida Provisória nº 2.187-13, de 24.8.2001 (DOU 27.8.2001) was in force on 11.9.2001, so it stays in force until a later MP revokes it or Congress votes on it (Emenda Constitucional 32/2001, art. 2); Medida Provisória nº 2.216, de 2001 (in force 2001-09-01) stands: Medida Provisória nº 2.216-37, de 31.8.2001 (DOU 1.9.2001, in force on publication), kept in force by Emenda Constitucional 32/2001, art. 2; its art. 33 revoked Lei 8.212 arts. 6, 7, 63 to 66, 77, 84 and 86 and Lei 8.213 arts. 7 and 8. Planalto's notes name this edition only, so the revocations are dated by its publication; earlier editions of the chain are not modelled; Medida Provisória nº 252, de 2005 (in force 2005-06-16) lapsed: Ato Declaratório do Presidente da Mesa do Congresso Nacional of 14.10.2005: 'teve seu prazo de vigência encerrado no dia 13 de outubro do corrente ano'; the wording it had replaced is back from 10.2.2009 (CF art. 62 § 3 makes a rejected MP lose effect from its edition; the history keeps its wording for the days Planalto shows it standing); Medida Provisória nº 447, de 2008 (in force 2008-11-17) was converted into Lei nº 11.933, de 2009 (in force 2009-04-29); - Lei nº 11.098, de 2005: in force 2005-01-14, art. 14: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor: I - a partir da data de publicação do ato referido no inciso I do art. 8º, para os arts. 1º, 2º, 3º e 4º; e II - a partir de 5 de outubro de 2004, para os demais artigos' (DOU 14.1.2005). The act of art. 8 I (creation of the Secretaria da Receita Previdenciária) is Decreto 5.256 of 27.10.2004 (DOU 28.10.2004, its Estrutura Regimental lists the Secretaria), published before the law, so art. 4 (the new wording of Lei 8.212 art. 39 caput) is in force from the law's own publication. Medida Provisória 222/2004, which the law converted and which had made the same change, is not noted on Planalto's page and is not modelled.
- Lei nº 11.457, de 2007: in force 2007-05-02, art. 51: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor: I - na data de sua publicação, para o disposto nos arts. 40, 41, 47, 48, 49 e 50 desta Lei; II - no primeiro dia útil do segundo mês subseqüente à data de sua publicação, em relação aos demais dispositivos' (DOU 19.3.2007): its changes to Leis 8.212 and 8.213 (arts. 2, 17, 32) fall under II, the first business day of May 2007 (1 May is a public holiday): 2.5.2007.
- Lei nº 12.873, de 2013: in force 2013-10-25, art. 63: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor: I - no 1º (primeiro) dia do sétimo mês subsequente à data de sua publicação, em relação ao art. 32-C da Lei nº 8.212 [...]; II - 90 (noventa) dias após a data de sua publicação, em relação: a) aos arts. 71-B e 71-C da Lei nº 8.213 [...]; e III - na data de sua publicação quanto aos demais dispositivos, produzindo efeitos a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2014, em relação: a) ao inciso VII do § 9º do art. 12, à alínea d do inciso I do § 11 do art. 12, e aos §§ 14 e 15 do art. 12 da Lei nº 8.212 [...]; b) ao inciso VII do § 8º do art. 11, à alínea d do inciso I do § 10 do art. 11, aos §§ 12 e 13 do art. 11 da Lei nº 8.213 [...]' (DOU 25.10.2013): I and II are dated by provision, III's effect days by the effect-days step.
- Lei nº 13.137, de 2015: in force 2015-06-22, art. 26 VII: the provisions not named in its incisos I to VI, which include art. 7 (Lei 8.212 art. 22 § 14), in force 'na data de sua publicação' (DOU 22.6.2015, edição extra).
- Lei nº 13.183, de 2015: in force 2015-11-05, art. 8: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor: I - em 3 de janeiro de 2016, quanto à redação do art. 16 e do inciso II do § 2º do art. 77 da Lei nº 8.213 [...]; II - em 1º de julho de 2016, quanto à redação do § 5º do art. 29-C da Lei nº 8.213 [...]; III - na data de sua publicação, para os demais dispositivos' (DOU 5.11.2015); the dispositivos of I and II are dated by provision.
- Lei nº 13.202, de 2015: in force 2015-12-09, art. 16: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor: I - a partir de 1º de dezembro de 2015 quanto ao art. 15; II - na data de sua publicação quanto aos demais dispositivos' (DOU 9.12.2015): its changes to Lei 8.212 (arts. 12 and 17) fall under II.
- Lei nº 13.467, de 2017: in force 2017-11-11, own clause: 120 days after publication (2017-07-14; LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1).
- Lei nº 13.670, de 2018: in force 2018-05-30, art. 11: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor: I - no primeiro dia do quarto mês subsequente ao de sua publicação, quanto aos arts. 1º e 2º, e ao inciso II do caput do art. 12; e II - na data de sua publicação, quanto aos demais dispositivos' (DOU 30.5.2018): its changes to Lei 8.212 (arts. 3 and 5) fall under II.
- Lei nº 13.756, de 2018: in force 2018-12-13, art. 47: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor: I - após decorridos 180 (cento e oitenta dias) [...] em relação à alteração do art. 18-A da Lei nº 9.615 [...]; e II - na data de sua publicação, em relação aos demais dispositivos' (DOU 13.12.2018): its change to Lei 8.212 (art. 36) falls under II.
- Lei nº 14.784, de 2023: in force 2023-12-28, art. 7: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor: I - na data de sua publicação, quanto aos arts. 1º, 2º, 4º e 5º; e II - no primeiro dia do quarto mês subsequente ao de sua publicação, quanto aos arts. 3º e 6º' (DOU 28.12.2023): its changes to Lei 8.212 (arts. 2 and 4) fall under I.
- Lei nº 8.540, de 1992: in force 1993-03-23, own clause: 90 days after publication (1992-12-23; LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1).
- Lei nº 9.983, de 2000: in force 2000-10-15, own clause: 90 days after publication (2000-07-17; LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1).
- Medida Provisória nº 258, de 2005: in force 2005-08-15, art. 38: 'Esta Medida Provisória entra em vigor: I - na data de sua publicação, em relação aos arts. 32 e 37; e II - em 15 de agosto de 2005, os demais artigos' (DOU 22.7.2005): its changes to Lei 8.212 (arts. 3, 27 and 39) fall under II.
- Medida Provisória nº 871, de 2019: in force 2019-01-18, art. 34 III: in force 'na data de sua publicação' (DOU 18.1.2019, edição extra) for every provision but its change to Lei 8.742/1993 art. 20 § 13 (art. 34 I, 90 days) and to Lei 8.213/1991 art. 74 § 3º (art. 34 II, 120 days).
- Medida Provisória nº 905, de 2019: in force 2019-11-12, art. 53: 'Esta Medida Provisória entra em vigor: I - noventa dias após a data de sua publicação, quanto às alterações promovidas pelo art. 28 nos art. 161, art. 634 e art. 634-A da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho [...]; II - no primeiro dia do quarto mês subsequente [...] quanto à inclusão do art. 4º-B na Lei nº 7.998, de 1990 [...]; e III - na data de sua publicação, quanto aos demais dispositivos' (DOU 12.11.2019); its changes to Leis 8.212 and 8.213 fall under III (its § 1º III: effects 'nas datas estabelecidas no caput').

- Effect days (produção de efeitos): where an act fixes a later day from which a provision produces effects ('produzindo efeitos a partir de ...'), the change is dated by that day, not by the act's in-force day (dates after 2026-10-31 are on the future branch); hunks a later act replaced before their effect day never took effect. Applied by Lexifina's code after the replay. - Acts of this part (Lei de Benefícios da Previdência Social (Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l8213cons.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Lei de Benefícios da Previdência Social (Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991): in force 1991-07-25 (Lei 8.213/1991 art. 155: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor na data de sua publicação' (DOU 25.7.1991, republished 11.4.1996 and 14.8.1998)).
- Headings (Parte, Livro, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- No OCR: every text comes from the HTML text layer of the Planalto pages.

- Life spans set by hand where Planalto's page cannot give them (Medidas Provisórias revoked, suspended by the STF or converted without the change): Lei 8.213: Medida Provisória 664/2014 (DOU 30.12.2014) put its changes in force on three days (art. 5): art. 60 §§ 5º-6º and art. 74 § 1º on publication (30.12.2014), art. 74 § 2º fifteen days after it (14.1.2015), the rest on 1.3.2015; all of them ended with its conversion into Lei 13.135/2015 (18.6.2015); Lei 8.213: Lei 13.135/2015 art. 6 II gave '2 (dois) anos' (to 19.6.2017) to 'a nova redação: a) do art. 16, incisos I e III, e do art. 77, § 2º, inciso IV [...] em relação às pessoas com deficiência intelectual ou mental'. Art. 77 § 2º IV (its wording, still in force) starts on 19.6.2017; its wording of art. 16 III was replaced by Lei 13.146/2015 (in force 3.1.2016) before that day and is left out (it never took effect); Lei 8.213 art. 77 § 2º II: Lei 13.146/2015 (in force 3.1.2016) and Lei 13.183/2015 (its art. 8 I: 'em 3 de janeiro de 2016, quanto à redação [...] do inciso II do § 2º do art. 77') both gave the inciso a wording from 3.1.2016; the later law's wording (Lei 13.183's) is the one in force from that day, and Lei 13.146's never applied (left out); Lei 8.213 art. 41 §§ 5º and 6º as enacted ('O primeiro pagamento de renda mensal [...]', 'O pagamento de parcelas [...]', no notes): renumbered §§ 6º and 7º by Lei 8.444/1992 (21.7.1992), which inserted a new § 5º; they had been dated by later rules; Lei 8.213 art. 74 § 3º: Planalto prints a struck bare label '§ 3º' with only '(Vide Medida Provisória nº 871, de 2019)' (MP 871's wording of the paragraph, in force 120 days after 18.1.2019 under its art. 34 II, is not printed); the line is left out and that wording is not modelled; Lei 8.213 art. 96: Lei 15.363/2026 (27.3.2026) added § 2º, so the parágrafo único (Lei 13.846/2019) became § 1º from then (the § 1º line carries only the 2019 note); Lei 8.213 art. 11 § 8º VI: Planalto leaves Lei 13.183/2015's wording unstruck above Lei 15.072/2024's ('Redação dada'); it ends on 27.12.2024; Lei 8.213 art. 106 I (Lei 11.718/2008's wording): Planalto strikes it with a style but gives no revocation note, and its consolidated page prints it as in force under Lei 13.846/2019's caput; it is kept.
- Twin wordings: a line printed below a struck line of the same dispositivo with the same start, word for word the same or (with no note of its own) a new wording, starts on the first day from the struck line's end on when no other wording of that dispositivo stands, or with the restored caput of its article; a struck lower copy that never stands alone is left out: lei-de-beneficios-da-previdencia-social art-011 [d)] second copy left out; lei-de-beneficios-da-previdencia-social art-015 [II -] repeated copy left out.
- A struck wording with no note and no later wording of the same label, printed above the lines that replaced it under new labels (a list renumbered or recast), ends when the first later wording below it in the same article starts (skipping later wordings of the sibling labels printed between them), credited to that wording's law: lei-de-beneficios-da-previdencia-social art-018 [] '2º O aposentado pelo Regime Geral de Pre' ends 1995-04-29; lei-de-beneficios-da-previdencia-social art-077 [II -] 'II - para o filho, a pessoa a ele equipa' ends 2019-06-18; lei-de-beneficios-da-previdencia-social art-096 [Parágrafo único] 'Parágrafo único. - Acts of this part (Código Brasileiro de Aeronáutica (Lei nº 7.565, de 19 de dezembro de 1986)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l7565.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Código Brasileiro de Aeronáutica (Lei nº 7.565, de 19 de dezembro de 1986): in force 1986-12-23 (Lei 7.565/1986 art. 323: 'Este Código entra em vigor na data de sua publicação' (DOU 23.12.1986, rectified 30.12.1986)).
- Headings (Parte, Livro, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- No OCR: every text comes from the HTML text layer of the Planalto pages.
- Some laws are in force on one day but defer the effects of some provisions ('produzirá efeitos'); a change is dated by the day it takes effect where the clause fixes a later day for it (the effect-days decision lists the units moved); effects that are retroactive, financial only or left to a later act or condition keep the in-force day. - Life spans set by hand where Planalto's page cannot give them (Medidas Provisórias revoked, suspended by the STF or converted without the change): Lei 13.932/2019 art. 15 I and II: art. 5 §§ 8º-9º (taxa de administração) are in force from 1.1.2020, and art. 20 XXI-XXII from 9.6.2020 (180 days after publication on 12.12.2019); art. 20 XXI as Medida Provisória 889/2019 had worded it (24.7.2019) ends when the conversion law gives the inciso its own wording (12.12.2019), so the inciso is absent from 12.12.2019 to 9.6.2020, as the clause defers it; art. 9 § 6º-A, also named in I, was vetoed; Lei 8.036 art. 3: Planalto notes both later wordings of the caput 'Redação dada pela Lei nº 9.649, de 1998'; Lei 9.649's own page shows that its art. 49 as enacted (27.5.1998) gave the caput with incisos I-VI ('integrado por três representantes da categoria dos trabalhadores [...]') and § 2º, and that Medida Provisória 2.216-37/2001 (DOU 1.9.2001) rewrote art. 49 to give the caput its present wording ('composto por representação de trabalhadores, empregadores e órgãos e entidades governamentais') and § 5º ('maioria simples'), and revoked § 2º (noted on this page). So the 1998 caput and its incisos stand from 28.5.1998 to 1.9.2001, the present caput and § 5º from 1.9.2001 (credited to MP 2.216-37; earlier editions of that MP chain are not modelled), and the 1990 § 5º to 1.9.2001; Lei 8.036 art. 13 § 5º I: Lei 13.446/2017's wording is replaced by Medida Provisória 889/2019's (24.7.2019); Lei 13.932/2019, the conversion, did not take up MP 889's § 5º and inciso I, and Planalto prints Lei 13.446's wording as today's text: it is out of force from 24.7.2019 to 12.12.2019; Lei 8.036 art. 23 § 2º: the 1990 caput and alíneas a)-b) give way to Medida Provisória 905/2019's § 2º (12.11.2019 to 20.4.2020, and again on 18.8.2020) and stand again from 20.4.2020 to 18.8.2020 and from 19.8.2020 to Medida Provisória 1.107/2022 (18.3.2022). Alínea c) as Medida Provisória 889/2019 added it (24.7.2019) ends when MP 905's § 2º starts (12.11.2019); its wording by Lei 13.932/2019 (MP 889's conversion, 12.12.2019) belongs to the 1990 § 2º and stands while that paragraph is in force (from 20.4.2020 to 18.8.2020 and from 19.8.2020 to 18.3.2022). Planalto prints the 1990 alíneas, MP 889's c) and Lei 13.932's c) twice, before and after MP 905's text; the second copy of MP 889's c) is left out.

- Acts of this part (Normas gerais de direito financeiro (Lei nº 4.320, de 17 de março de 1964)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l4320.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Normas gerais de direito financeiro (Lei nº 4.320, de 17 de março de 1964): in force 1964-05-07 (Lei 4.320/1964 has no vigência clause (its art. 114 counts its effects from 1.1.1964 for the budgets and from 1.1.1965 for the rest): LINDB art. 1, 45 days after publication in the DOU of 23.3.1964 (rectified 9.4.1964 and 3.6.1964); the vetoed parts Congress kept were promulgated in the DOU of 5.5.1964, before that day).
- Headings (Parte, Livro, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- No OCR: every text comes from the HTML text layer of the Planalto pages.

- Acts of this part (Marco Regulatório das Organizações da Sociedade Civil (Lei nº 13.019, de 31 de julho de 2014)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l13019.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Marco Regulatório das Organizações da Sociedade Civil (Lei nº 13.019, de 31 de julho de 2014): in force 2016-01-23 (Lei 13.019/2014 art. 88 as worded by Lei 13.204/2015: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor após decorridos quinhentos e quarenta dias de sua publicação oficial, observado o disposto nos §§ 1º e 2º deste artigo' (DOU 1.8.2014; the 540th day counted from publication is 22.1.2016, LC 95/1998 art. 8 § 1); its § 1º: 'Para os Municípios, esta Lei entra em vigor a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2017' (§ 2º: earlier by local act). The original term (90 days) was extended by MP 658/2014 and Lei 13.102/2015 (360 days) and MP 684/2015 (540 days) before it ran out).

- Acts of this part (Lei da Assistência Judiciária (Lei nº 1.060, de 5 de fevereiro de 1950); Lei do Protesto de Títulos (Lei nº 9.492, de 10 de setembro de 1997); Intervenção e liquidação extrajudicial de instituições financeiras (Lei nº 6.024, de 13 de março de 1974); Lei da Identificação Criminal (Lei nº 12.037, de 1º de outubro de 2009)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l1060.htm, l9492.htm, l6024.htm, l12037.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).

- Some laws are in force on one day but defer the effects of some provisions ('produzirá efeitos'); a change is dated by the day it takes effect where the clause fixes a later day for it (the effect-days decision lists the units moved); effects that are retroactive, financial only or left to a later act or condition keep the in-force day. - Medida Provisória 955/2020 (DOU 20.4.2020, art. 1: 'Fica revogada a Medida Provisória nº 905, de 11 de novembro de 2019') is not noted on every page that notes Medida Provisória 905/2019; where it is not (Lei 12.037 art. 2 II), the change MP 905 made is still dated by the CLT's MP 905/955 sequence: in force 12.11.2019, undone while MP 955 stood (20.4.2020 to its lapse on 18.8.2020), in force again on 18.8.2020, MP 905's last day, and undone from 19.8.2020, when MP 905 lapsed. Planalto prints the line MP 905 revoked twice, struck with MP 905's note and again unstruck; the unstruck copy is the line from 19.8.2020 (lei-da-identificacao-criminal art-02 [II -]).
- Medidas Provisórias 905/2019 and 955/2020: MP 905/2019 (DOU 12.11.2019, its changes to this act in force on publication, art. 53 III) was revoked by MP 955/2020 (DOU 20.4.2020, in force on publication); MP 955 lapsed on 17.8.2020 (Ato Declaratório do Presidente da Mesa do Congresso Nacional nº 113, de 2020), so MP 905 had effect again on 18.8.2020, the last day of its own term (Ato Declaratório nº 127, de 2020). Planalto prints each MP 905 wording twice (struck 'Revogada pela Medida Provisória nº 955, de 2020' for the first period, struck 'Vigência encerrada' for the second): each stands from 12.11.2019 to 20.4.2020 and again on 18.8.2020, credited to MP 905 and to the end of MP 955's term; the wordings MP 905 replaced or revoked stand again from 20.4.2020 to 18.8.2020 and from 19.8.2020 (as in the CLT): lei-da-identificacao-criminal art-02 [II -]: revoked by MP 905, gap while MP 955 stood.
- Life spans set by hand where Planalto's page cannot give them (Medidas Provisórias revoked, suspended by the STF or converted without the change): Lei 6.024 art. 19: Medida Provisória 784/2017 (8.6.2017) rewrote the article (caput, incisos I-II with alíneas a)-f), §§ 1º-7º); it lapsed on 19.10.2017 and the 1974 article was in force again from 20.10.2017 until Lei 13.506/2017 (14.11.2017). - Acts of this part (Imposto de renda das pessoas físicas (Lei nº 9.250, de 26 de dezembro de 1995)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l9250.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Imposto de renda das pessoas físicas (Lei nº 9.250, de 26 de dezembro de 1995): in force 1995-12-27 (Lei 9.250/1995 art. 41: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor na data de sua publicação' (DOU 27.12.1995)).
- Headings (Parte, Livro, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- No OCR: every text comes from the HTML text layer of the Planalto pages.
- Some laws are in force on one day but defer the effects of some provisions ('produzirá efeitos'); a change is dated by the day it takes effect where the clause fixes a later day for it (the effect-days decision lists the units moved); effects that are retroactive, financial only or left to a later act or condition keep the in-force day. - L9250: lines found alive before the law their note names: 0.
- Lines that close a quoted amendment ('....." (NR)', a quoted article, or a sentence ending with the closing quotation mark) are kept in the article that quotes them; the marginal-heading rule, which moves an unlabelled line without closing punctuation into the next article, does not apply to them (2 lines).
- Lei 9.250: the centred titles of the tables Lei 15.270/2025 added in arts. 3º-A and 11-A ('Tabela de redução do imposto mensal', '... do ajuste anual') are lines of those articles, not headings; empty centred lines are left out; the name lines of Capítulos II-A and III-A start with the 'CAPÍTULO' line above them, which carries Lei 15.270's note; Planalto's marker 'Sem eficácia' after the struck lines of Medida Provisória 252/2005 in art. 22 is not part of the text ('Tabela de redução do imposto mensal' -> art-03-a; empty centred line dropped; 'DA TRIBUTAÇÃO MENSAL DE ALTAS RENDAS' dated with 'CAPÍTULO II-A'; 'Tabela de redução do ajuste anual' -> art-11-a; 'DA TRIBUTAÇÃO ANUAL DE ALTAS RENDAS' dated with 'CAPÍTULO III-A'; art-22 marker 'Sem eficácia' left out of the text).
- Struck items printed with a label and only the note '(Vide Medida nº 340, de 2006)', and no words, are pointers, not wordings, and are left out (l9250 art-04 'a).', l9250 art-04 'b).', l9250 art-04 'c).', l9250 art-04 'd).', l9250 art-10 'a).', l9250 art-10 'b).', l9250 art-10 'c).', l9250 art-10 'd).').
- Tables printed inside articles (l9250 4, l9250-compilado 3): Planalto centres their cells; each cell is a line of the article it is printed in (as in the CLT's art. 580), not a heading line.
- A period printed after an amendment note that follows a line already ending in ';', ':' or ',' ('... salário-maternidade; (Redação dada pela Lei nº 9.528, de 10.12.97).') closes the note and is dropped with it (lines: l9250 7).
- Lei 9.250 (open items): changes whose effects reach back before their in-force day keep that day (Medida Provisória 2.189-49/2001 art. 12, Medida Provisória 22/2002 and Leis 10.451/2002, 11.119/2005, 11.196/2005 art. 38, 11.311/2006, 11.324/2006, 11.482/2007, 11.727/2008 art. 21, 12.469/2011 and 12.832/2013); 'Vide' pointers (Medidas Provisórias 340/2006 and 1.303/2025, Leis 9.532/1997, 13.043/2014 and others) strike no words and are not modelled; earlier editions of Medida Provisória 2.189-49 are not modelled.
- Life spans set by hand where Planalto's page cannot give them (Medidas Provisórias revoked, suspended by the STF or converted without the change): Lei 9.250 art. 4: Medida Provisória 1.171/2023 (in force 1.5.2023) revoked the parágrafo único (art. 15 II) and added §§ 1º and 2º (art. 14); it lapsed on 27.8.2023 (Ato Declaratório nº 62/2023), and Lei 14.663/2023 (DOU 28.8.2023, edição extra, in force on publication) art. 6 numbered the parágrafo único as § 1º, with new wordings of § 1º and its incisos and a § 2º, the same day the parágrafo único would have come back. So the parágrafo único and its incisos I and II (Lei 13.202/2015) end on 1.5.2023 and do not come back (Planalto leaves inciso I unstruck); the struck § 2º with no note is MP 1.171's (read on the MP's page), 1.5.2023 to the lapse; Lei 9.250 art. 22 caput: Medida Provisória 252/2005 (in force 16.6.2005) gave it a new wording and lapsed on 13.10.2005; the 1995 wording stands again from 14.10.2005 until Lei 11.196/2005 (in force 22.11.2005; its art. 38 has effects from 14.10.2005, a retroactive effect: the change keeps its in-force day). Planalto prints the 1995 caput once, struck; Lei 9.250 art. 8 II c) item 9: Planalto prints Medida Provisória 670/2015's wording unstruck above Lei 13.149/2015's (its conversion law, same words); MP 670's line ends on 22.7.2015.

- Medidas Provisórias and their fate, from each MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line or the Congress records: Medida Provisória nº 1.171, de 2023 (in force 2023-05-01) lapsed: Ato Declaratório do Presidente da Mesa do Congresso Nacional nº 62, de 2023 (DOU 31.8.2023): 'teve seu prazo de vigência encerrado no dia 27 de agosto de 2023'; the wordings it had replaced are back from 28.8.2023; Medida Provisória nº 2.189, de 2001 (in force 2001-08-24) stands: Medida Provisória nº 2.189-49, de 23.8.2001 (DOU 24.8.2001; in force on publication), kept in force by Emenda Constitucional 32/2001, art. 2; its art. 11 gave Lei 9.250 arts. 10 and 25 new wordings (its art. 12 applies the art. 10 wording to taxable events from 1.1.1998, a retroactive application: the change keeps its in-force day). - Acts of this part (Imposto de renda (Lei nº 7.713, de 22 de dezembro de 1988)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l7713.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Imposto de renda (Lei nº 7.713, de 22 de dezembro de 1988): in force 1989-01-01 (Lei 7.713/1988 art. 57: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor em 1º de janeiro de 1989' (DOU 23.12.1988, the day LexML gives; the page footer misprints 23.12.1998)).
- Headings (Parte, Livro, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- No OCR: every text comes from the HTML text layer of the Planalto pages.
- Some laws are in force on one day but defer the effects of some provisions ('produzirá efeitos'); a change is dated by the day it takes effect where the clause fixes a later day for it (the effect-days decision lists the units moved); effects that are retroactive, financial only or left to a later act or condition keep the in-force day. - Acts of this part (Legislação tributária federal (Lei nº 9.430, de 27 de dezembro de 1996)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (l9430.htm), with the replay of Lexifina's code (imported, not copied): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
- Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.
- A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
- Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).
- Legislação tributária federal (Lei nº 9.430, de 27 de dezembro de 1996): in force 1996-12-30 (Lei 9.430/1996 art. 87: 'Esta Lei entra em vigor na data da sua publicação, produzindo efeitos financeiros a partir de 1º de janeiro de 1997' (DOU 30.12.1996): financial effects only, so the in-force day).
- Headings (Parte, Livro, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.
- Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
- The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.
- No OCR: every text comes from the HTML text layer of the Planalto pages.
- Some laws are in force on one day but defer the effects of some provisions ('produzirá efeitos'); a change is dated by the day it takes effect where the clause fixes a later day for it (the effect-days decision lists the units moved); effects that are retroactive, financial only or left to a later act or condition keep the in-force day.
